A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Any-to-Bokeh research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-benchmark results, component ablations, real-video demonstrations, and a user study with 24 participants and 480 ratings.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional evaluations, ablations, computational comparisons, and a user study with 51 participants and 1020 ratings.

M1.justification: The main MPI-guided SVD architecture, three-stage training, and cosine overlap strategy remain. Appendix A.6.3 introduces Ours-tiny, a smaller student trained through knowledge distillation from the full model. This is a limited method extension; the extensive rewriting does not establish a replacement of the main architecture.

E1.justification: The synthetic matting-based data and DAVIS coverage remain, and noisy-depth testing already existed in v1. A limited coverage removal is the explicit demonstration on video-generator-produced inputs in v1 Figure 1, which is absent from v2's replacement figure and remaining evaluations.

E2.justification: V2 adds BokehDiff (Zhu et al., 2025) to the main quantitative comparison, user study, and qualitative comparisons. DeepLens, BokehMe, Dr.Bokeh, and MPIB remain. BokehDiff is distinct from the Fortes et al. Bokeh Diffusion work already cited in v1.

E3.justification: V2 introduces VEPI evaluation using DAVIS foreground masks, increases the user study from 24 participants/480 ratings to 51/1020, and adds multi-step-denoising, blending, and distilled-model controls. Appendix A.6.3 adds single-frame computational profiling on an H800. The core training settings and 200-video synthetic test set remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds one-step versus retrained multi-step diffusion, linear versus cosine blending, cross-method noisy-depth comparisons, and a distillation efficiency/quality analysis. Existing pretrained-prior and temporal-refinement ablations are retained in Tables 5–6 rather than newly introduced. V1's demonstrated missing-depth failure case is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The larger user-study sample and new relative-performance-drop percentages change evaluation size and results, not uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the previous scores, including Any-to-Bokeh's PSNR of 38.899, but adds BokehDiff results and VEPI scores, with Any-to-Bokeh scoring 0.944. User-study percentages are replaced under the expanded study, including 60.3% to 77.8% preference against Dr.Bokeh. Tables 3 and 7–9 add multi-step, blending, noisy-depth, and distilled-model results; these are additional evaluations, not evidence of improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: V2 formally defines the foreground-ROI VEPI metric in Appendix A.4. It also changes the second overlap-frame index from j in v1 Equation (5) to j+L in v2 Equation (6), and changes the stated interval restriction from d_f to 1/d_f. These are localized mathematical changes; the main MPI and loss formulations remain.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly claims the first dedicated diffusion framework for video bokeh and emphasizes state-of-the-art in-focus boundary fidelity. V1 described a novel framework and included a generalization claim 'without domain-specific training,' which is dropped. The central controllable, temporally coherent video-bokeh contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 removes Appendix C's substantive limitation that missing disparity structures can cause incorrect defocus because of the synthetic-to-real gap, together with its proposed remedies. It adds interpretations concerning multi-step flicker, blending, noisy-depth robustness, and computational tradeoffs. Removing the explicit failure boundary while emphasizing robustness materially changes the qualification of the findings.

D1.justification: V2 adds parameter/FLOP disclosures, single-frame H800 profiling details, and qualifications about custom CUDA renderers. It omits v1's explicit CLIP semantic-injection, Sobel-operator, and skip-connection convolution descriptions. The main training hyperparameters remain, and a future code-release promise is added without documenting a completed release.

R1.justification: V2 adds Zhu et al.'s BokehDiff and Joseph et al.'s edge-preservation work, while removing Wan, CogVideoX, and several references supporting one-step diffusion and 3D priors. The broad positioning against classical/image-based bokeh remains, with a more explicit first-dedicated-video-diffusion novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and much of the method narrative are extensively rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized around focal-plane-adapted MPI representation before the diffusion backbone, and the appendix gains a contents page and nested sections. The title, author list, publication header, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the teaser and replaces multiple qualitative comparison figures, including the failure illustration. Table 1 gains a comparator and metric, while v1 Table 3 is redistributed across v2 Tables 3, 5, and 6; additional analyses appear in Tables 7–9. These changes substantially reshape the visual presentation beyond the conference-template conversion.

improvement.justification: The added diffusion baseline, one-step versus multi-step control, and quantitative real-video evaluation strengthen support for the central method beyond v1. These benefits are tempered by removal of the documented missing-depth failure case and overstatement of the blending result: Table 7 favors linear blending on flow difference (0.422 versus 0.431), despite claiming superior temporal consistency for cosine blending. The stronger evidence supports a limited net improvement.
